overview.text: The Red-banded Snake is a medium-sized, non-venomous, night-active snake of East Asia. The Reptile Database now places it in the genus *Dinodon*.

identification.text: A long, fairly flat head, slightly bulging eyes with vertical pupils, and red bands along the body.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually about 70 cm long, rarely up to 130 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Much of East Asia, from Korea (and just into Russia) through eastern China to northern Laos and Vietnam, plus Taiwan and the Ryukyu Islands.

habitat.text: Many habitats from near sea level to about 2,000 m, most common on river plains. Usually on the ground, but it sometimes swims in streams.

diet.text: Hunts at night for fish, frogs, lizards, other snakes and young birds.

recognise.text: Red bands on a dark body.
